verdicts.quote: “The LinkedIn API uses OAuth 2.0 for member (user) authorization and API authentication.”
verdicts.reason: Marketing APIs require member authorization via OAuth 2.0, so OAuth2 is the primary auth. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/authentication?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and select partners at its discretion…”
verdicts.reason: You can self‑serve an app, but meaningful Marketing/Ads access is granted after LinkedIn’s review, matching app_review. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/marketing-tiers?view=li-lms-2026-04&utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “The platform offers APIs to create LinkedIn marketing campaigns, to report campaign performance, to manage leads, and to grow a company Page.”
verdicts.reason: Docs cover many areas (campaign management, targeting, analytics/reporting, lead sync, community management), indicating broad coverage. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/marketing-integrations-overview?view=li-lms-2026-07))

verdicts.quote: “Not affiliated with or endorsed by LinkedIn.”
verdicts.reason: There is no official MCP from LinkedIn, but community MCP servers exist; thus value should be community, not none. ([github.com](https://github.com/aigamer-dev/linkedin-mcp?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “LinkedIn has two tiers of access to our Advertising API: Development and Standard.” … “LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and select partners at its discretion…”
verdicts.reason: Public docs and OAuth make it buildable now, but access is review/tier‑gated (and other constraints apply), so ready_with_caveats is appropriate. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/marketing-tiers?view=li-lms-2026-04&utm_source=openai))
